response.internal_assessment: Things feel pretty normal right now. The shop is steady, cars keep coming in, and I'm keeping up with the work. My savings aren't huge but I'm getting by okay — four months of runway if something went sideways, which I try not to think about too hard. The computer diagnostics side of things is something I've been leaning into more lately. Most of the older guys here still do a lot of it by feel, but I can pull codes and trace electrical faults faster than most of them. I don't know if that matters long-term, but it feels like something. I just take it one week at a time, honestly.

chosen_actions.description: Complete standard repair queue at the shop — brake jobs, oil changes, one transmission diagnostic. Normal productive day.
chosen_actions.reasoning: This is just the job. Show up, do good work, get paid. No reason to deviate from routine when everything is stable.

chosen_actions.description: Spend about an hour after work watching a YouTube series on advanced OBD-II diagnostics and CAN bus fault tracing — something a coworker mentioned offhand last week.
chosen_actions.reasoning: I heard someone mention CAN bus issues are getting more common on newer vehicles. It's not a formal plan, more just curiosity — and it ties into the electrical and computer stuff I'm already decent at. Low effort, probably useful. I'd rather be doing something with my hands but this is close enough.

response.emotional_state: Calm and steady. A little flat maybe — not unhappy, just... going through the motions in a way that feels comfortable. The work is satisfying when something clicks. Mild background hum of financial worry that I mostly keep at arm's length.
response.archetype_self_assessment: I'm a person who does her job well and doesn't make a lot of noise about it. I'm not someone who maps out five-year plans. I like fixing things. I'm good at it. That feels like enough most days.
response.inner_monologue: Okay, transmission on the Civic first — that code it threw is probably just the shift solenoid, I've seen that three times this month. Then the brake job on the F-150, that one's straightforward. Maybe grab lunch from that taco truck if it's out front today. After work I'll look up that CAN bus stuff — Marcus mentioned it and he's usually on to something when he brings up tech. I'm not worried about the future right now. Things are fine. Things are fine.
